questions.question: Distracted drivers are more likely to crash when using which of the following?
questions.explanation: Cell phones, hands-free phones, radios, and CD players can all distract you while driving. These distractions increase your risk of crashing.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop when a flagger, stop sign, gates, or flashing lights tell you to. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey before the other three?
questions.explanation: Police officers can direct traffic. Their directions take priority over all signs, signals, and road markings. Traffic directors include police officers, fire police, construction flaggers, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: You may drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road:

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in any vehicle on a public road. You also cannot have open containers in the areas where the driver or passengers sit.

questions.question: If your tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes immediately.
Gradually slow down and pull off the road.

questions.explanation: If you have a blowout, remove your foot from the gas. Do not brake right away. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the road ahead is divided. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs show:
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you about railroad crossings. Yield to trains and never try to race across the tracks.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways at the intersection.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A triangular red and white yield sign means slow down and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be prepared to stop if you need to.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This creates space in front of your vehicle for them to pass. The other driver will pass in less time and more safely.

questions.question: When you approach an accident scene, what should you do?

options.text: Stop only if you are involved or if emergency help is not there yet.

questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not stop just to look at accidents, fires, or disasters.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot every time you change your vehicle's position. Check your blind spots before turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers were looking but still did not see the motorcyclist, bicyclist, or pedestrian. These road users are smaller and harder to spot. They may move faster and have less noticeable lights. Always watch for them to prevent collisions.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "be careful." When you see this light, slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle approaching from the right.
The vehicle approaching from the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, you must yield to a vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle will hit in a crash.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to see through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Check if your blind spot is clear. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, make sure the passing lane is clear. Give the proper turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.

questions.explanation: Every quick stop wastes fuel because you must accelerate again to match traffic speed. If you look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes, you can avoid sudden braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing the intersection.
Always come to a complete stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. If traffic is heavy, you must stop completely at a yield sign.

questions.question: Hurricane evacuation route signs:

options.text: Mark highways to use if a hurricane evacuation is ordered.
Are only posted when a hurricane is happening.
Are only for visitors from out of state.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mark highways to use if a hurricane evacuation is ordered.
questions.explanation: Hurricane evacuation route signs show which highways to use in an emergency. Know where these signs are located in case you need to evacuate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming ahead.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or backward so the driver can see you.
Honk your horn to warn them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or backward so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never drive in someone else's blind spot. Move ahead or drop back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Get back in your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Turn on your signal before changing lanes. Return to your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When traffic lights are sideways, where is the green light?
questions.explanation: Some cities have sideways traffic lights. The red light is on the left, yellow is in the middle, and green is on the right.

questions.question: In snowy weather, what should happen to your following distance?
questions.explanation: In bad weather, slow down and increase the space between your car and the car ahead. It takes longer to stop on icy roads than on dry roads.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means you can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
You may only proceed if a green arrow and a green circle appear together.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means you can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go, but traffic in that lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?

options.text: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
Large trucks need less distance to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more space to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where large vehicles do not block your view of traffic ahead.
